section_2_claim_fidelity.verdict: Wordings are FAITHFUL — in five of six cases near-verbatim from the ledger, with no drift in any number or scope. Limitations are the weak point: three claims lose limitations the ledger attaches to them, in a document that states its own rule as 'Nothing here may be quoted without the limitation attached to it' (README line 39-40). That internal inconsistency is required item R3.
section_2_claim_fidelity.the_six_readme_surfaced_claims: Confirmed by reading the ledger in full: exactly six claims carry "README" in surfaces — CX-H1-PRIMARY, CX-CAPGAP-01, CX-GROUNDING-01, CX-SEALED-01, CX-COST-01, CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01. All six appear in the README. None is missing.

per_claim.CX-H1-PRIMARY: Wording: VERBATIM from the ledger, including the operating point ('At a target risk of 20% with 95% confidence and a 20% acceptance floor'). All three limitations carried in the same paragraph: the H1/H2 collapse, the no-invented-difference rule, and the dual scoping to in-domain RAMS and the frozen vLLM 4-bit stack. This paragraph is the best-executed one in the change. Defect is in its BOLD HEADER, not its body — see required item R2.
per_claim.CX-CAPGAP-01: Wording: faithful. The ledger's 'The infeasibility reflects a capability gap rather than a limitation of the certification method' is compressed to the header 'The failure is capability, not method' and the quantitative half is verbatim ('with an unlimited threshold grid, no finite-sample penalty and oracle threshold selection ... at most 2.0% of documents at 20% empirical error, against a required 20%'). BOTH limitations carried, in the same paragraph: 'a diagnostic that selects no threshold and certifies nothing', and 'the same diagnostic on the development split gives 3.0%, so the conclusion reproduces out of sample'. CLEAN.
per_claim.CX-GROUNDING-01: Wording: verbatim on every figure (95.7 / 39.4 / 68.1 / 5,355 -> 340). Limitations 1 and 2 carried in the same passage and carried well — '"Valid" means parseable and grounded, not correct — a span can point at real document text and still name the wrong entity or role' and 'must never be reported without that null attached'. This satisfies docs/plan3/certification-result.md's Permitted clause requiring the figure to appear 'in the same document and the same passage as the null'. Limitation 3, 'Scoped to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack', is NOT in the passage; it appears only 40 lines later under 'What this is not'. Minor but real — see R3.
per_claim.CX-SEALED-01: Wording: VERBATIM. Its single limitation (final/shift descoped for absence of a selected policy, not cost or effort) is carried — but in the Status section, ~50 lines above the claim, not attached to it. Acceptable; the substance travels. The ledger's tail clause 'both commands are free to run' is dropped, which is the specific phrasing that forecloses a 'they ran out of money' reading. Noted, not required.
per_claim.CX-COST-01: Wording: VERBATIM including the em-dash list and the CPU-at-no-cost clause. Limitation 'Approximate: individual job costs are recorded exactly, the total is rounded' is carried implicitly by 'approximately'. Limitation 'Excludes the value of free-tier and local compute' is DROPPED entirely and appears nowhere in the README — see R3. This matters more than it looks: '$19 for the entire programme of GPU work' invites a total-cost-of-research reading that the dropped limitation exists to block.
per_claim.CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01: Wording: faithful; the numbers (~16x, 0.017, 0.000, 87%) match and the causal clause is verbatim. Three of six limitations carried, and the three carried are the three that matter most: descriptive-only, the counterfactual is NOT uniformly generous, and the baselines rest on an arithmetic ceiling rather than the counterfactual. This is impressive discipline — those three are exactly what the reanalysis reviewer's R5 forced. Three are dropped: (a) grounding-oracle coverage is not a deployable acceptance rate and is not comparable across systems — harmless here, since the README quotes movements and not the 0.0374 coverage; (b) 'the certificate bounds average within-group loss, not the absence of error in any document (ADR 0009)' — harmless here, since the README claims no certificate; (c) 'The QLoRA system sits below that ceiling, so for it the ceiling is silent and only the measured curve leaves it short'. (c) is the problem: evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json re_review_2026_07_22.claim_boundaries_unchanged_except.amendment_1 states that this distinction 'must travel with the claim'. The README carries the baseline half ('for the baselines the conclusion rests on an arithmetic ceiling') and drops the QLoRA half. See R3. The pointer 'See the claim's limitations field before citing it' is a good instinct but is not a substitute for the one limitation a reviewer explicitly ordered to travel.

section_3_forbidden_wordings.verdict: CLEAN on all eight. I walked the 'Forbidden — in both directions' table in docs/plan3/certification-result.md line by line against the full README text, in both columns, and also against evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json claim_boundaries.may_not_be_said. No forbidden wording is present, in substance or by implication — with ONE unscoped-summary qualification recorded under required item R1, which I rule a calibration defect rather than a forbidden wording.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.imply_a_laxer_alpha_would_certify: NOT PRESENT. The strongest test available: the README omits the alpha-frontier entirely, so there is no crossing value from which a reader could infer a reachable target, and it nowhere describes 0.20 as strict, conservative, aggressive, or chosen. It states the target as fact and moves on. CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.quote_95_7_without_the_null_attached: NOT PRESENT, and defended in three places. The document's second paragraph is 'The answer, on RAMS, is no — and that null is the result'. The 95.7% paragraph itself carries 'This improvement did not translate into a certified selective guarantee, and must never be reported without that null attached'. 'What this is not' repeats it. The figure cannot be lifted from this document without the null coming with it. CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.call_grounding_validity_accuracy: NOT PRESENT. The word 'accuracy' occurs once, in the negation: 'Not an accuracy claim. The 95.7% grounding figure is validity, not correctness'. The claim paragraph independently states '"Valid" means parseable and grounded, not correct'. CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.present_a_diagnostic_as_a_certificate: NOT PRESENT. Both diagnostics carry the disclaimer inline: 'This is a diagnostic that selects no threshold and certifies nothing' (CX-CAPGAP-01) and 'The decomposition is descriptive: it selects no threshold and certifies nothing' (CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01). CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.claim_to_have_discovered_CRC_extraction_: NOT PRESENT. The README cites no prior work at all, makes no novelty claim about certification failing on extraction, and frames its own contribution as gate discipline plus a null. CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.claim_mu_0_60_replicates_or_refutes_2606: NOT PRESENT. No mu figure, no citation, no comparison to any external result anywhere in the file. CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.generalise_past_the_frozen_stack_or_in_d: NOT PRESENT; the README over-corrects if anything. Scoping appears at least five times: 'Scoped to in-domain RAMS and to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack' in the H1 paragraph, 'The answer, on RAMS' in the lede, and two dedicated 'What this is not' bullets. CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.state_a_certified_margin: NOT PRESENT, and actively foreclosed: 'so no comparison of certified acceptance between them is possible', 'no numerical difference is computed against an infeasible baseline', and 'no certified acceptance is claimed for any system'. CLEAN.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.also_checked_overclaiming_the_null_colum: 'QLoRA doesn't work' is NOT present and is affirmatively refuted — 'QLoRA produced a large, real gain — in the wrong property'. The reanalysis reviewer's may_not_be_said items are also clean: the README does not call the grounding oracle 'the most generous reading' (it says the opposite, correctly); it does not present '+0.0000' as a general property of grounding counterfactuals (it attributes the baselines' result to the arithmetic ceiling); it does not say the infeasibility is 'not an artefact of the operating point'; it calls nothing a certificate.
section_3_forbidden_wordings.the_one_qualification: The lede at README line 8 — 'The answer, on RAMS, is no' — answers a two-part question posed one line above, the first part of which is method-shaped ('whether a document-level abstention policy can certify bounded extraction risk while retaining useful coverage'). Stripped of the operating point, that sentence generalises the null across operating points, which is the mirror image of the forbidden 'a laxer alpha would certify' and sits against the reanalysis reviewer's may_not_be_said entry 'That the infeasibility is not an artefact of the operating point full stop. It is not an artefact of a NARROWLY chosen one.' The operating point IS given, correctly and verbatim, 34 lines later. I rule this a lede-calibration defect (R1), not a forbidden wording — it makes no affirmative statement about other alphas — but it is the sentence most likely to be quoted alone and it is the first required item for that reason.

The pending half is stated as though it were a gate; ADR 0011 §6 says in terms that it 'is a regression tripwire, not a verification gate, and the name must not be read as evidence the hole is closed', catching 7 of 18 realistic pending strings and missing 11. The README's next clause ('The known limits of that check are written down in ADR 0011 §6 rather than left implied by the function's name') partly discharges this by pointing at the limits — which is why this is a nit and not a BLOCK — but the README's own sentence commits the error the ADR warns against before pointing at the warning.

section_5_second_source_of_truth.verdict: YES, it creates one — and the repo already contains the machinery that exists to prevent exactly this. This is the most consequential structural finding in the review, though it is a nit in severity because nothing is currently wrong.
section_5_second_source_of_truth.the_machinery_that_is_being_bypassed: src/conformalextract/claims.py defines `render_surface(ledger, surface)` whose docstring reads: 'Render the approved sentences for one surface, each with its limitations attached. Deliberately mechanical: public prose is assembled from approved wordings rather than re-written, so a claim cannot drift from the sentence its evidence supports.' It emits every claim for a surface followed by every one of its limitations. tests/test_claims.py::test_render_surface_emits_approved_wording_with_limitations already calls it with surface='README'. The README change hand-writes the six README-surfaced claims as prose instead — which is the drift mechanism render_surface was written to make impossible, and the three dropped limitations under R3 are precisely the lines render_surface would have emitted and did not get the chance to.
section_5_second_source_of_truth.no_mechanism_pins_the_two_together: There is no test asserting that README.md carries the claim IDs the ledger surfaces to README, nor that it carries their limitations. tests/test_doc_references.py covers README.md but only for `test_*` identifier resolution — it would not notice a ledger wording change, a limitation addition, a surface being revoked, or a claim ID appearing in the README that the ledger does not surface there. So the README and the ledger can diverge silently, and the ledger has already been amended three times in one day (2026-07-22) under reviewer pressure.
where_it_goes_stale_first: The Plan 3 row, 'not formally closed — no Plan 3 close record exists'. This is the fastest-decaying sentence in the file: it is falsified by the creation of a single JSON file in evidence/plan3/, which is a routine next step.
'The next unit of work is the write-up, which is not started.' Falsified by the first draft commit.

'348 tests pass' — mitigated but not solved by the commit anchor. A reader at a later HEAD sees a number that is both stale and, because 6cfd947 will not be HEAD once this README itself is committed, anchored to a commit that is not the tip.
'reviewed over four independent passes' — a fifth pass is appended to the same record file, and the count in the README does not move.
'approximately $19 against a $25 ceiling' — falsified by any future paid run.
The six claim paragraphs — they duplicate ledger wording and ledger limitations verbatim, so any ledger amendment silently desynchronises them.
The 0.017 / 0.000 / 87% / 2.0% / 3.0% figures also duplicate docs/plan3/certification-result.md, giving those numbers three homes.
section_5_second_source_of_truth.recommendation_not_required: Either generate the Result section from `render_surface(load_ledger(...), 'README')` at doc-build time, or add a test in tests/ that asserts (a) every claim ID cited in README.md is surfaced to README in the ledger, and (b) every claim the ledger surfaces to README appears in README.md. (a) alone would have caught required item R2 mechanically. I am not requiring this because it is new engineering and would exceed the scope of a README commit; I am recording it so it is not lost, and R8 records the minimal version.

section_6_under_and_over_claiming.verdict: The change corrects a genuine and serious under-claim, and does NOT over-correct into over-claiming. The residual defects are calibration and attribution, not inflation.
section_6_under_and_over_claiming.the_defect_it_exists_to_fix_is_genuinely: The replaced text said 'Plan 1 is active; training, certification claims, and publication remain blocked until their preceding independent review passes.' At 6cfd947 every clause of that was false: Plan 1 completed 2026-07-17, Plan 2 closed 2026-07-21, certification executed and was reviewed 2026-07-22, and the publication condition on derived claims was LIFTED in the third reanalysis pass. Continuing to publish it would itself have been a false statement on a public surface. The correction is warranted and is not gold-plating.
section_6_under_and_over_claiming.over_correction_check: I looked specifically for standing or certainty the evidence does not support, and did not find it. The README claims no certification, no margin, no portability, no accuracy, no reproducibility-on-CPU, no shift result, no novelty against prior work, and no gate advance. Every number I could trace traces. The two places that read as strongest are 'The answer, on RAMS, is no' (R1) and 'The gate discipline is the substantive engineering contribution here' — the latter is an editorial self-assessment rather than an evidence claim, and I do not require its removal, but it is the one sentence in the file that a hostile reader would call puffery and it is not covered by any claim ID.
section_6_under_and_over_claiming.residual_under_selling: Two, both in the safe direction, both recorded rather than required. (1) 'still blocked on six discipline and wording items' understates R1 of that BLOCK, which was a live sealed-label hole: cli._load_reanalysis_splits accepted an arbitrary --roles string with no guard, so `--roles final` would have opened the sealed split and then written `final_reads: 0` into the artifact. The reviewer's own words were 'a missing guard combined with a machine-readable false attestation'. Calling that a 'discipline and wording item' is the strongest available argument for the repo's review culture and the README gives it away — see R7. (2) 'the reviewer confirmed every number by from-scratch reimplementation' is marginally stronger than the record supports: the record says 'Every value ... that I recomputed', the citation checks were done by independent web fetch rather than reimplementation, and one parenthetical ('(10/14)'/'(3/14)') is recorded as NOT confirmed. Also R7.

required_items._note: Ranked by severity. All are stated so they can be discharged without further interpretation. None requires new analysis, new evidence, or a new gate. R1-R4 are substantive; R5-R7 are accuracy corrections; R8 is the structural recommendation reduced to its minimum enforceable form.

R1_attach_the_operating_point_to_the_led.current: The answer, on RAMS, is **no** — and that null is the result, established under a procedure built before the sealed labels were opened.
R1_attach_the_operating_point_to_the_led.what_is_wrong: The preceding sentence poses two questions, the first of which is method-shaped ('whether a document-level abstention policy can certify bounded extraction risk while retaining useful coverage'). An unqualified 'no' answers it across all operating points. CX-H1-PRIMARY's approved wording carries the operating point as part of the claim, and evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json claim_boundaries.may_not_be_said forbids stating that the infeasibility is 'not an artefact of the operating point full stop'. The operating point is present in the document but 34 lines below, and this is the sentence most likely to be quoted alone — which the README's own rule at line 39-40 ('Nothing here may be quoted without the limitation attached to it') forbids.
R1_attach_the_operating_point_to_the_led.what_it_should_say: Carry the operating point and the scope in the sentence itself, e.g.: 'At the operating point this project froze before opening any sealed label — 20% target risk, 95% confidence, 20% acceptance floor — the answer on in-domain RAMS is **no**, for every system tested; and that null is the result, established under a procedure built before the sealed labels were opened.' Any wording that binds the 'no' to the frozen operating point discharges this.

R2_do_not_attribute_a_three_system_headl.current: **No system could be certified** (`CX-H1-PRIMARY`). At a target risk of 20% with 95% confidence and a 20% acceptance floor, neither the QLoRA-adapted system nor the zero-shot baseline could be certified on RAMS…
R2_do_not_attribute_a_three_system_headl.what_is_wrong: CX-H1-PRIMARY covers two systems. The third (few-shot) is CX-H2-SECONDARY, whose `surfaces` are ["report"] and do NOT include README. The sentence is true and is permitted by evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.certification.json, but a three-system assertion is labelled with a two-system claim ID in the one document whose stated purpose is that every statement carries the ID that licenses it.
R2_do_not_attribute_a_three_system_headl.what_it_should_say: Either (a) narrow the header to the claim, e.g. '**Neither the adapted system nor the zero-shot baseline could be certified** (`CX-H1-PRIMARY`)'; or (b) keep 'No system could be certified' and cite its actual authority — `CX-H1-PRIMARY` plus `CX-H2-SECONDARY` — and add CX-H2-SECONDARY's first limitation in the same passage ('reported jointly with CX-H1-PRIMARY as one finding, never as an independent second confirmation'), which the README already effectively carries. Option (b) additionally requires adding "README" to CX-H2-SECONDARY's `surfaces` in evidence/plan4/claim_ledger.json — which is a claims change and therefore needs its own independent review under CLAUDE.md. Option (a) needs no ledger change and is the cheaper discharge.

R3_carry_the_limitations_the_ledger_atta.what_is_wrong: The README states at lines 39-40 that 'Nothing here may be quoted without the limitation attached to it' and then drops limitations the ledger attaches. Three are material: (a) CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01 limitation 4, 'The QLoRA system sits below that ceiling, so for it the ceiling is silent and only the measured curve leaves it short' — evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json re_review_2026_07_22.claim_boundaries_unchanged_except.amendment_1 states that this distinction 'must travel with the claim'; the README carries only the baseline half. (b) CX-COST-01 limitation 1, 'Excludes the value of free-tier and local compute' — dropped entirely; without it '$19 for the entire programme of GPU work' invites a total-cost-of-research reading. (c) CX-GROUNDING-01 limitation 3, 'Scoped to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack' — present in the document but not in the passage, unlike the other two limitations of the same claim which are correctly in-passage.
R3_carry_the_limitations_the_ledger_atta.what_it_should_say: (a) After 'for the baselines the conclusion rests on an arithmetic ceiling rather than on the counterfactual', add: 'The QLoRA system sits below that ceiling, so for it the ceiling is silent and only the measured curve leaves it short.' (b) Append to the Cost paragraph: 'The figure excludes the value of free-tier and local compute; individual job costs are recorded exactly and the total is rounded.' (c) Add 'Scoped to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack.' to the CX-GROUNDING-01 paragraph, as the H1 paragraph already does for itself.

R4_per_job_cost_is_not_recorded_to_the_c.current: - **Per-job cost recorded to the cent**, against a hard aggregate ceiling enforced in code (`training.REMAINING_BUDGET_USD`), with a run ledger imposing R0→R1→R2 order.
R4_per_job_cost_is_not_recorded_to_the_c.what_is_wrong: Not supported by the records, and unledgered. Actual recorded costs are a mix of precisions: docs/plan2/serving-equivalence-probe-result.md gives $0.046 and $0.48 (to the cent or better), but docs/progress.md records the Gate 0E and both Gate 0F jobs as 'about $0.05', docs/plan2/g2b-result.md gives '~$0.10', and docs/plan2/r2-launch-brief.md gives 'Programme spend to date ≈ $6.85'. I found no committed artifact holding a per-job cost ledger at cent precision. Overstating the precision of the cost discipline is the same class of error the rest of this section is written to avoid.
R4_per_job_cost_is_not_recorded_to_the_c.what_it_should_say: '**Per-job cost recorded in each run's evidence artifact**, against a hard aggregate ceiling enforced in code (`training.REMAINING_BUDGET_USD` = $24.7992, the $25 cap less $0.2008 of prior recorded spend), with a run ledger imposing R0→R1→R2 order.' Optionally note that the aggregate is rounded, which R3(b) already requires in the Cost paragraph.

R5_the_LF_canonicalisation_note_is_attac.current: …e.g. Gate 0F at `adb61606…`, pinned to Hub revision `840fb41e…`. Hashes are taken over git-canonical (LF) bytes; a Windows working copy hashes differently and the correction is recorded rather than left as a trap.
R5_the_LF_canonicalisation_note_is_attac.what_is_wrong: The LF-canonicalisation correction is correction C3 of evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.certification.json and applies specifically to the certification artifact sha256 `71c0de3e…` (docs/plan3/certification-result.md, 'Hash canonicalisation (correction C3)', with the CRLF value `55237e5a…`). `adb61606…` is a Gate 0F Hub-download hash; no record establishes that it is over LF-normalised bytes. Juxtaposing them states a general policy that is documented for one hash and asserts it of another. The README also never cites `71c0de3e…`, the hash the note actually belongs to, so a reader necessarily attaches it to the wrong one.
R5_the_LF_canonicalisation_note_is_attac.what_it_should_say: Split the two facts. Keep the Gate 0F example as a cross-storage-boundary match (Hub artifact vs in-Git evidence copy, `adb61606…` at Hub revision `840fb41e…`). Then state the canonicalisation against its own hash: 'The certification artifact is pinned at `71c0de3e…` over git-canonical (LF) bytes; a Windows working copy is checked out CRLF and hashes differently, and that correction is recorded (`docs/plan3/certification-result.md`) rather than left as a trap for an independent verifier.'

R6_state_the_pending_rule_as_the_tripwir.current: - **Claims cannot outrun their evidence.** `conformalextract verify-claims` fails closed if a claim's evidence is not git-tracked, or if it holds a public surface while its own verification is recorded as pending. The known limits of that check are written down in ADR 0011 §6 rather than left implied by the function's name.
R6_state_the_pending_rule_as_the_tripwir.what_is_wrong: The tracked-evidence half is exactly right. The pending half is stated as a gate. ADR 0011 §6 says: 'The pending rule is a regression tripwire, not a verification gate, and the name must not be read as evidence the hole is closed' — measured against 18 realistic strings it catches 7 and misses 11, including 'under review', 'in progress' and 'verification outstanding'. The README's own following sentence points at those limits, which is why this is a nit; but the sentence commits the error before pointing at the warning against it.
R6_state_the_pending_rule_as_the_tripwir.what_it_should_say: '- **Claims cannot outrun their evidence.** `conformalextract verify-claims` fails closed if a claim's evidence is not git-tracked, and a regression tripwire refuses a claim that holds a public surface while its own verification literally reads as pending. The tripwire is not a verification gate and does not claim to be — what it catches and what it misses is measured and written down in ADR 0011 §6 rather than left implied by the function's name.'

R7_two_narrative_precision_fixes_in_the_.current: …on the ADR 0011 re-analysis, where the reviewer confirmed every number by from-scratch reimplementation and still blocked on six discipline and wording items.
R7_two_narrative_precision_fixes_in_the_.what_is_wrong: Two inaccuracies, both understating the record. (1) 'six discipline and wording items' mischaracterises R1, which was a live sealed-label hole: `cli._load_reanalysis_splits` accepted an arbitrary `--roles` string with no guard, so `--roles final` would have opened the sealed split while the artifact attested `final_reads: 0`. The reviewer's own framing was 'a missing guard combined with a machine-readable false attestation'. (2) 'confirmed every number by from-scratch reimplementation' is stronger than the record: it says 'Every value … that I recomputed', the citation checks were done by independent web fetch rather than reimplementation, and one parenthetical ('(10/14)', '(3/14)') is recorded as NOT confirmed.
R7_two_narrative_precision_fixes_in_the_.what_it_should_say: '…on the ADR 0011 re-analysis, where the reviewer reproduced the load-bearing numbers by from-scratch reimplementation with zero mismatches and still blocked on six items — including a `--roles` hole that would have let a sealed split be opened while the artifact attested zero reads of it.' Optionally soften 'closing at PASS' at line 30 to 'closing with the publication condition lifted and no blocking items', which is what evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json re_review_3.publication_status and re_review_4.required_items_none_blocking actually record.

R8_pin_the_README_to_the_ledger.what_is_wrong: The README now hand-writes six claims that `claims.render_surface(ledger, 'README')` exists to emit mechanically — its docstring says 'public prose is assembled from approved wordings rather than re-written, so a claim cannot drift from the sentence its evidence supports'. Nothing pins them together: tests/test_doc_references.py covers README.md only for `test_*` identifier resolution, so a ledger amendment, a revoked surface, or a claim ID cited in the README that the ledger does not surface there would all pass silently. The ledger was amended three times in one day on 2026-07-22.
R8_pin_the_README_to_the_ledger.what_it_should_say: Minimum enforceable form, and the only part I require: a test asserting that every `CX-…` claim ID appearing in README.md is present in evidence/plan4/claim_ledger.json AND carries "README" in its `surfaces`. That check alone would have caught R2 mechanically. The stronger converse (every README-surfaced claim appears in README.md) and the fuller move (generating the Result section from `render_surface`) are recommended but not required — they are new engineering beyond a README commit, and generating prose from the ledger may not be worth the loss of readability.
R8_pin_the_README_to_the_ledger.if_deferred: If the author prefers not to add a test in this commit, R8 may instead be discharged by recording it as an open item in docs/plan3/HANDOFF-2026-07-22-reanalysis.md as a dated appended note. It must not be silently dropped: the divergence risk is real and the machinery to close it already exists in the repo.

The six claims it carries were already authorised for the README surface by evidence/plan4/claim_ledger.json and by the lifting of the publication condition in evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json re_review_3_2026_07_22.

R8_test_adjudication.why_this_got_the_hardest_look: The author disclosed that the first version of this regex was wrong and that a mutation probe — not reading — is what caught it. That is the correct instinct and it is also a warning: a test that gives false assurance is the exact failure ADR 0011 §6 records for the pending tripwire. I therefore verified every property by probe, in a throwaway loop that saved README.md's bytes, mutated them, ran the single test node, and restored. sha256 before and after: a0f1feda3972335a37a1238977c60db4df164c9582b38fa53f13bde8728e93a1, IDENTICAL. Nothing was left modified.
R8_test_adjudication.probe_2_unsurfaced_id: FIRES ON THE RIGHT ASSERTION. Appending a `CX-H2-SECONDARY` citation to README.md produced exit 1 with: 'AssertionError: README.md cites claims the ledger does not surface to \'README\': [\'CX-H2-SECONDARY\']. Either remove them from the document or add the surface in the ledger -- and a ledger change is a claims change, which needs its own independent review.' This is the `unsurfaced` assertion, NOT the `unknown` one — which is the discriminating outcome, since CX-H2-SECONDARY IS in the ledger and the failure must be about its surfaces. The bug the author found in their own first draft is genuinely fixed: the old `CX-...-\d+` pattern could not see this ID at all. The assertion message also names the correct remedy and correctly flags that the ledger route needs its own review.
R8_test_adjudication.probe_3_unknown_id: FIRES ON THE RIGHT ASSERTION. Appending `CX-TOTALLY-INVENTED-99` produced exit 1 with: 'AssertionError: README.md cites claim IDs absent from the ledger: [\'CX-TOTALLY-INVENTED-99\']'. The `unknown` assertion precedes the `unsurfaced` one in source order, so an ID that is both unknown and unsurfaced reports as unknown — which is the more informative diagnosis. Correct ordering.

probe_4_brittleness_of_the_anchor_stripp.verdict: SAFE, NOT A LATENT TRAP — and I say so on probe evidence, not on reading. The degradation mode is LOUD.
probe_4_brittleness_of_the_anchor_stripp.what_the_derivation_actually_does: `claims.CLAIM_ID` is `re.compile(r"^CX-[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)*$")`. `CLAIM_ID.pattern.strip("^$")` yields `CX-[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)*`. Note `str.strip` takes a character SET, so it also survives doubled or reordered anchors.
probe_4_brittleness_of_the_anchor_stripp.measured_against_four_rewordings_of_the_: Current `^CX-[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)*$` -> extracts all six README IDs including CX-H1-PRIMARY. A `(?:...)` non-capturing reword -> same six (and `group(0)` makes the capture-group question moot either way, which is why the author's `finditer`+`group(0)` choice is right and `findall` would have been wrong). A `^CX-[A-Z0-9-]+$` character-class reword -> same six. A `\ACX-...\Z` reword -> ZERO matches, because `strip("^$")` does not remove `\A`/`\Z`.
probe_4_brittleness_of_the_anchor_stripp.probe_of_the_only_failing_case: I probed the observable consequence of that zero-match case by stripping every claim ID out of README.md and running the test: exit 1, 'AssertionError: README.md cites no claim IDs; the regex or the document has changed / assert set()'. So the `assert cited` guard on line 179 catches precisely the degradation the anchor-stripping could produce. The test cannot silently stop matching.
probe_4_brittleness_of_the_anchor_stripp.ruling: This is the difference between this test and the pending tripwire ADR 0011 §6 warns about: the tripwire fails OPEN (misses 11 of 18 and says nothing), this test fails CLOSED (any loss of matching power trips the emptiness guard). The `assert cited` line is not decoration — it is the whole safety argument, and it works. I would not have required it; the author included it unprompted.

R8_test_adjudication.probe_5_the_converse_is_not_asserted: CONFIRMED BY PROBE, and omitting it is defensible. I replaced the `(\`CX-SEALED-01\`)` citation in README.md with '(claim omitted)' and re-ran: 1 passed. So removing a README-surfaced claim from the README does not fail the test — the direction asserted is one-way, exactly as the module comment states. Defensible for the reason the comment gives: the ledger is the authority on what MAY be said, not on what MUST be said, and adding a surface to the ledger should not break an unrelated commit. Asserting the converse would make the README a mandatory publication target for every future ledger amendment, which inverts the doctrine — the ledger constrains prose, prose does not constrain the ledger.
residual_gaps_recorded_not_required: The test is a CITATION check, not a claim-detection oracle. Prose can assert something claim-shaped without citing an ID and escape it entirely — the R1 lede is itself an example (three-system statement, no ID). This is inherent and not fixable by a regex; I record it so nobody later mistakes a green test for 'the README is claim-safe'. Human review remains the gate for uncited prose, which is what this record is.

The unanchored pattern has no `\b` boundary, so an ID embedded in a longer uppercase token could match a prefix. Any such match would be reported as `unknown` and fail loudly, so the failure mode is a false positive, not a false negative. Not worth fixing.
`PUBLIC_PROSE_SURFACES` is a one-entry dict parametrized over its keys, so adding `model_card` or a report path later is a one-line change. Good shape.
